from.place: Proof, passage from a finite affine etale covering family to its disjoint union and its Cech complex

title: Cech complex of a finite affine etale covering and its disjoint union
statement: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $(u_i:U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ be a finite jointly surjective family of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] with every $U_i$ affine, and let $F$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Set $V=\coprod_{i\in I}U_i$ and $u:V\to X$. Then $V$ is affine, $u$ is surjective, etale, and the corresponding ring map $A\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. For every $p\ge0$ the sheaf property identifies $F(V\times_X\cdots\times_XV)$ (with $p+1$ factors) with $\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}}F(U_{i_0}\times_X\cdots\times_XU_{i_p})$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. These isomorphisms commute with all face restrictions and therefore identify the Cech complexes [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] of the one-map cover $\{V\to X\}$ and the family $(u_i)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03OZ (label lemma-cech-complex), for a standard etale covering; proof including equation label equation-sheaf-coprod

proof.text: The coproduct $V=\coprod_{i\in I}U_i$ is affine because it is a finite disjoint union of affine schemes, by clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. The induced map $u:V\to X$ is etale by [lem-sc-etale-coproduct-etale]. It is surjective because the images of the coproduct summands are the images of the $u_i$, whose union is all of $X$ by joint surjectivity. Since an etale morphism is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism], the induced ring map $A\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. The surjectivity of $u$ says that the induced map on the points of the affine spectra is surjective; hence this flat ring map is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat].

source.place: Lemma Tag 03OZ (lemma-cech-complex), proof: finite coproduct of affine schemes; the induced map is etale and surjective; faithful flatness of the corresponding ring map

proof.text: For every $p\ge0$, the fibre-product distribution isomorphism [lem-sc-etale-fibre-product-coproduct] gives $$V\times_X\cdots\times_XV\cong\coprod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}}U_{i_0}\times_X\cdots\times_XU_{i_p}.$$ Each summand is an object of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], since it is an iterated fibre product of etale objects.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03OZ (lemma-cech-complex), proof and equation label equation-sheaf-coprod

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] the coproduct summands of the right-hand side of step 2 map to it by open immersions whose images cover it; open immersions are etale by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], so these inclusions form a finite covering in $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Apply the equalizer sheaf axiom in [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] to this covering. Distinct summands have empty fibre product by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and an abelian sheaf takes the empty object to the zero group (the empty covering equalizer). Therefore the equalizer is the product of the section groups on the summands, giving $$F(V\times_X\cdots\times_XV)\cong\prod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}}F(U_{i_0}\times_X\cdots\times_XU_{i_p}).$$

source.place: Lemma Tag 03OZ, equation label equation-sheaf-coprod and the sheaf axiom for the covering by coproduct summands

proof.text: The isomorphisms in step 3 commute with the face restrictions: by [lem-sc-etale-fibre-product-coproduct], the face projection of the coproduct fibre product restricts on each indexed summand to the face projection of the corresponding $U_{i_0}\times_X\cdots\times_XU_{i_p}$. Contravariance of $F$ therefore carries the componentwise product identification through every restriction map. By the definition of the Cech complex in [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex], the degreewise products and alternating face maps are exactly the Cech complexes of the one-map cover $\{V\to X\}$ and of the family $(u_i)$, so the identifications give an isomorphism of Cech complexes.
